question.text: Merchants from this empire and the later Songhai Empire partook in the trans-Saharan trade. This empire's ruler Mansa Musa disrupted the Egyptian economy by handing out gold during his trip to Mecca.
question.clue: That founder defeated the Sosso monarch Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.

swap.text: This Mali emperor, a nephew of Sundiata, caused massive devaluation of gold due to his extremely lavish hajj, during which he supposedly built a mosque every Friday.
swap.clue: The architect es-Saheli built the Djinguereber Mosque for this man, who also commissioned Sankore University.

question.leadin: The Islamic Courts Union once controlled much of the southern part of this country, but in 2006 it splintered into groups like al-Shabaab.
question.text: Name this country on the Horn of Africa. It has been considered a failed state for its inability to control a civil war in its territory or piracy in its waters.
question.clue: After the dictator Siad Barre was ousted from power in this nation, warlords began to take control of autonomous regions such as Puntland.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of South Africa.
swap.text: This is the term for the segregation policy of South Africa from 1948 to the 1990's.
swap.clue: It became harsher during Hendrik Verwoerd's prime ministership with the creation of ten Bantustan "homelands."

question.text: The northern part of this modern-day country was ruled by the Kingdom of Axum. This country's emperors included Menelik II and Haile Selassie, the Rastafarian Messiah.
question.answerHtml: Ethiopia [or ītiyop’iya; or Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia; or YeEtiyop’iya]
question.clue: This country contains the Chapel of the Tabot in the city of Axum, which supposedly houses the ark of the covenant.

swap.leadin: Many of this nation's cities, which have black 'townships' at their fringes, have 'grayed', for which its government has done 'willing-buyer, willing-seller' land reform.
swap.text: Name this southernmost African nation whose three capitals are Bloemfontein, Johannesburg, and Cape Town. The De Beers family of companies began here.
swap.clue: In that song, musicians pledged to not play at a casino resort in this country, "Sun City".

question.leadin: Answer some questions about an African empire.
question.text: This empire had its capital at Gao, and its first great king Sonni Ali repressed the scholars of Timbuktu.
question.clue: Forces of this empire were lead by Ishaq II when it lost to Moroccan forces at Tondibi.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the African leaders of the 1980s.
swap.text: Samuel Doe served as president of this country throughout the 1980s. His successor would later sever and eat his ear on tape before plunging this country ruled by an elite descended from American immigrants into a civil war.
swap.clue: Perhaps its most controversial leader declared his "national unification policy" and announced an "open door policy," constructing the largest mercantile fleet in the world.

question.text: This son of Nandi and Senzangakona forged the Zulu empire through military innovations like the buffalo horns formation and the iklwa spear, which replaced the assegai.
question.clue: The iklwa was a shortened version of the assegai promoted by this commander, who was succeeded by Dingane after his assassination.

swap.text: 250 people were killed in this 1960 incident during a Pan-Africanist Congress protest of apartheid. Nelson Mandela chose the site of this event to sign the 1996 South African constitution.
swap.clue: The site of this event was where the new constitution was formally ratified in 1996.

question.leadin: The combatants in the Toyota War of the late 1980s had a disputed border along this geographical area.
question.text: Name this strip of land between Chad and Libya.

swap.leadin: After becoming prime minister at the age of only 33 under president Jean-Baptiste Ouedraogo, this leader was placed under house arrest by Francois Mitterand's son Jean-Christophe.
swap.text: Identify this Marxist Pan-Africanist who was sometimes known as "Africa's Che Guevara."
swap.clue: He symbolically rode in a beat-up Renault 5 instead of a Mercedes, ordered millions of trees to be planted on the Sahel, and saw his country attacked by Mali in the 1985 Agacher Strip War.

question.leadin: Subordinate states like Zafun practiced the serpent cult of this empire, which emerged from Oualata and other cities built by the Neolithic Tichitt civilization after the "big dry" period.
question.text: Name this early Sahelian empire whose bipartite capital described by al-Bakri may be Kumbi Saleh ("KOOM-bee SAH-leh"), Mauritania. Takrur and the Almoravids possibly sacked this empire's city of Aoudaghost before its 13th-century disintegration.
question.answerHtml: Ghāna Empire [or Wagadou; or Awkâr; or Kingdom of ancient Ghāna]
question.clue: This empire was the first in its region to treat all gold nuggets larger than dust as its king's property.

swap.leadin: Identify the following presidents of South Africa.
swap.text: This strong supporter of apartheid, proceeded De Klerk as State President of South Africa, serving from 1985 to 1989, and continuing the South African policy of intervention in Angola.
swap.clue: In 1984, Mozambique concluded the Nkomati Accord with this South African Premier who was known as "the old crocodile."

question.text: After his deposition, Nkrumah sought refuge in this country, of which he was made honorary co-president. This Francophone country was ruled after independence by Ahmed Sekou Toure.
question.clue: This country's largest city, port, and capital is split across the Camayenne Peninsula and Tombo Island in the southwest, and was attacked in Operation Green Sea.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about embarrassing revelations from the November 2010 leaked diplomatic cables scandal involving the whistleblower website WikiLeaks.
swap.text: Ronald McMullen, American Ambassador to this country, described its capital Asmara as a disgusting, run-down Italian colonial outpost with a sinister atmosphere reminiscent of an Evelyn Waugh novel.
swap.clue: This country's south contains the border town of Badme, which was occupied in a conflict that ended after a 2018 coffee ceremony.

question.text: This mercenary of Irish blood was hired by Moise Tshombe to put down the Simba rebellion in the Congo. In 1981, he and his drinking buddies in Ye Ancient Order of Froth Blowers created a fake rugby team that tried to overthrow the president of the Seychelles; that plan failed.
question.answerHtml: Mike Hoare [or Thomas Michael Hoare; or Mad Mike Hoare]

swap.leadin: Name these African leaders who assembled impressive Rolls Royce collections.
swap.text: This leader customarily greeted crowds in his red Rolls Royce, which he used to pick up Elizabeth II ("the-second") from an airport. He took the title mwazi or "savior" and banned hippies from entering Malawi during his long tenure.
swap.clue: This politician, who enforced his litany of restrictive social policies through a non-communist Young Pioneers organization. This politician chose the modern name of his country, which replaced "Nyasaland."

question.leadin: Name these cities which serve as effective world capitals, FTPE.
question.text: This was the capital of Cote d'Ivoire from 1933 to 1983, succeeding Bingerville in that role, and remains by far its largest city, with over three million residents.
question.clue: Longtime Ivorian president Felix Houphouet-Boigny ["oo-foo-EH bwahn-YEE"] moved the capital to Yamoussoukro from this city, which remains the most populous in Cote d'Ivoire.

swap.text: Under Amin's term many peoples were massacred, including this ethnic group, a subgroup of the Luo peoples. Famous Ugandans of this ethnicity include Okot p'Bitek and the leader of the Lord's Resistance Army, Josef Kony.
swap.clue: This Luo-speaking ethnic group in South Sudan and northern Uganda, who form the core of the Lord's Resistance Army. The only Ugandan president of this ethnic group, Tito Okello Lutwa, was deposed by Yoweri Museveni ("YAH-wair-ee MUH-seh-veh-nee").
